title: Cider mussels and cabbage on toast

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Mussels, cider, butter, shallots, garlic, cabbage, crème fraîche and bread are all plain home ingredients with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Bagged live mussels, dry cider and the rest are everyday stock at Tesco at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: One lidded pan and a toaster are ordinary kit, and steaming and shelling mussels is within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: Steaming 1kg of mussels in 150ml cider, softening half a cabbage, then reducing the liquor and adding crème fraîche gives a well-balanced topping for four slices of toast at lunch.

honest_times.reason: Thirty-five active minutes covers scrubbing, shelling, slicing and stirring the cabbage, and the 5 minutes of steaming plus a short reduction roughly fits the 10 printed cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the parsley and pepper, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used apart from the toast made from the listed bread.

seasonal_feel.reason: Half a white cabbage is a main component alongside October mussels in a warm autumn lunch, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: Short, clear British phrasing such as 'binning any open ones' reads like a neighbour explaining.

hearty_healthy.reason: Mussels, cabbage and crusty toast make a filling lunch with real protein and vegetables.
